data.name: S0.Title
data.value: Most often confused

data.name: S0.Intro
data.value: Words that look alike but mean different things in Vyxum.

data.name: T0.01.Name
data.value: Batch and lot

data.name: T0.01.Text
data.value: Both can mean a group of goods made together. In Vyxum, batch appears in three places: in Formulation, one mixing of a recipe; in Net weight control, the group of packages judged together (for example one hour of production); and the batch number printed on the label. Lot usually means the raw material batch written on the supplier's sack.

data.name: T0.02.Name
data.value: Tare and zero

data.name: T0.02.Text
data.value: Zero sets the empty scale's display back to 0 (dust left on it, drift). Tare subtracts the weight of the container or packaging so that the net weight shows. The zero command goes to the scale; in Vyxum the tare is kept in the software.

data.name: T0.03.Name
data.value: Qn and fill target

data.name: T0.03.Text
data.value: Qn is the quantity printed on the label (250 g). The fill target is what the filling machine aims for, usually a little more (253 g). Net weight control checks against Qn.

data.name: T0.04.Name
data.value: Tolerance and TNE

data.name: T0.04.Text
data.value: Tolerance is the acceptance range the company sets itself (for example target ± 5 g). TNE is the negative error the regulation allows; it is not typed in but calculated from Qn.

data.name: T0.05.Name
data.value: Calibration and verification stamp

data.name: T0.05.Text
data.value: Calibration measures and documents how far the scale is off, using reference weights. The verification stamp is when an authorised body approves and seals the scale for use in trade. One is technical, the other is legal.

data.name: T0.06.Name
data.value: Best before and use by

data.name: T0.06.Text
data.value: The best before date is about quality: after it the product is not dangerous but may lose freshness. The use by date is about safety for products that spoil quickly: after it the product must not be eaten.

data.name: T0.07.Name
data.value: Package, case, pallet

data.name: T0.07.Text
data.value: A package is the single pack the consumer buys. A case is the outer box that holds several packages. A pallet is the wooden base the cases are stacked on. Each can have its own label.

data.name: S1.Title
data.value: Weighing basics

data.name: S1.Intro
data.value: Scale, weight and calculation. The words behind every screen.

data.name: T1.01.Name
data.value: Scale / indicator

data.name: T1.01.Text
data.value: The hardware that weighs. On an industrial scale the platform that measures and the box with the display (the indicator) can be separate; the computer connects to the indicator by cable or over the network.

data.name: T1.01.InVyxum
data.value: The Devices screen and the setup wizard.

data.name: T1.01.Example
data.value: The text "Scale 1 connected".

data.name: T1.02.Name
data.value: Station

data.name: T1.02.Text
data.value: The place where one operator works: scale, screen and, if there is one, a printer. The Vyxum license is counted per station.

data.name: T1.02.InVyxum
data.value: Label numbers and cases are counted per station.

data.name: T1.02.Example
data.value: The "Packing 2" station.

data.name: T1.03.Name
data.value: Gross

data.name: T1.03.Text
data.value: The total weight of everything on the scale: the product plus the container or packaging.

data.name: T1.03.InVyxum
data.value: A weighing record keeps gross, tare and net separately.

data.name: T1.03.Example
data.value: 1.260 kg including the pack.

data.name: T1.04.Name
data.value: Tare

data.name: T1.04.Text
data.value: The weight of the container, box or packaging. It is subtracted from the gross to find the real product weight. "Take tare" makes whatever is on the scale now the tare.

data.name: T1.04.InVyxum
data.value: "Take tare" on the Weighing screen; the packaging tare on the product card is applied when the product is chosen.

data.name: T1.04.Example
data.value: Empty bag 0.012 kg.

data.name: T1.05.Name
data.value: Net

data.name: T1.05.Text
data.value: The weight of the product itself. Net = gross − tare.

data.name: T1.05.InVyxum
data.value: The large number on the screen is usually the net; the amount and the label are based on the net.

data.name: T1.06.Name
data.value: Zero

data.name: T1.06.Text
data.value: Making the display start from 0 while the scale is empty. It is not the same as tare (see Most often confused).

data.name: T1.06.InVyxum
data.value: The "Zero" button; a single command goes to the scale. Vyxum sends no other setting commands to the scale.

data.name: T1.06.Example
data.value: If the empty scale shows 0.002, zero it.

data.name: T1.07.Name
data.value: Stable / unstable

data.name: T1.07.Text
data.value: A weight that has settled is stable; one that is still moving is unstable. An unstable weight is not saved.

data.name: T1.07.InVyxum
data.value: "stable" or "moving" on the Weighing screen.

data.name: T1.07.Example
data.value: A pack is put down and settles a second later.

data.name: T1.08.Name
data.value: Max, Min, e

data.name: T1.08.Text
data.value: Max is the largest load the scale can carry (capacity). Min is the smallest weighing that counts as reliable. e (the division) is the smallest step of the display.

data.name: T1.08.Example
data.value: Max 6 kg, Min 40 g, e = 2 g.

data.name: T1.09.Name
data.value: Overload / underload

data.name: T1.09.Text
data.value: The weight is above or below the range the scale can measure. The reading cannot be trusted then.

data.name: T1.09.InVyxum
data.value: The record is refused.

data.name: T1.10.Name
data.value: Weighing range

data.name: T1.10.Text
data.value: Which weights a scale is used for.

data.name: T1.10.InVyxum
data.value: Formulation sends each ingredient to the scale whose range fits its target.

data.name: T1.10.Example
data.value: Scale 2: 0 to 0.5 kg; small additives are weighed there.

data.name: T1.11.Name
data.value: Target weight

data.name: T1.11.Text
data.value: The weight a package or ingredient should have.

data.name: T1.11.InVyxum
data.value: On the product card (optional) and in the recipe; the vertical line on the gauge.

data.name: T1.11.Example
data.value: Target 1,000 g.

data.name: T1.12.Name
data.value: Tolerance / tolerance band

data.name: T1.12.Text
data.value: How far below or above the target is allowed. The band runs from target − tolerance to target + tolerance. The company sets it.

data.name: T1.12.InVyxum
data.value: Shown as a box on the gauge. In Formulation, "Confirm" stays closed outside the band.

data.name: T1.13.Name
data.value: Deviation

data.name: T1.13.Text
data.value: The difference between what was weighed and the target.

data.name: T1.13.InVyxum
data.value: The batch complete screen and reports.

data.name: T1.13.Example
data.value: Target 50 kg, weighed 50.12 kg: +0.12 kg (0.24%).

data.name: T1.14.Name
data.value: Mean (x̄) and standard deviation (s)

data.name: T1.14.Text
data.value: The mean is the average weight of a group of packages. The standard deviation shows how far the packages spread around the mean; if it is small, filling is even.

data.name: T1.14.InVyxum
data.value: The net weight quality screen and the compliance report.

data.name: T1.15.Name
data.value: PLU

data.name: T1.15.Text
data.value: The product's short code (Price Look-Up). Used to call up the product quickly and to put it in the weight barcode.

data.name: T1.15.InVyxum
data.value: The code field on the product card; search by PLU on the Weighing screen.

data.name: T1.15.Example
data.value: Pistachios: 00417.

data.name: T1.16.Name
data.value: Unit price / amount

data.name: T1.16.Text
data.value: The unit price is the price per kilogram. Amount = net × unit price.

data.name: T1.16.InVyxum
data.value: The Weighing screen and the retail label.

data.name: T1.17.Name
data.value: Calibration

data.name: T1.17.Text
data.value: Testing the scale with known weights (reference weights) to measure and document how far it is off. It is adjusted if needed.

data.name: T1.17.Example
data.value: A 5 kg weight is put on and the scale shows 5.002.

data.name: T1.18.Name
data.value: Verification stamp / periodic inspection

data.name: T1.18.Text
data.value: A scale used in trade is inspected and sealed by an authorised body. It is renewed at set intervals. A scale without a valid stamp cannot be used for legal weighing.

data.name: T1.18.InVyxum
data.value: The stamp date on the compliance report; Net weight control needs a legal measuring instrument.

data.name: T1.18.Example
data.value: The inspection sticker and seal on the scale.

data.name: T1.19.Name
data.value: Legal measuring instrument

data.name: T1.19.Text
data.value: A measuring instrument under state control because it is used for sales or legal declarations. Its settings must not be changed.

data.name: T1.19.InVyxum
data.value: This is why Vyxum sends the scale only read and zero commands.

data.name: S2.Title
data.value: Products and production

data.name: S2.Intro
data.value: Product card, recipe and batch: the language of production.

data.name: T2.01.Name
data.value: Product card

data.name: T2.01.Text
data.value: A product's main data: code (PLU), name, unit price, packaging tare, target weight; for labels, shelf life and ingredients.

data.name: T2.01.InVyxum
data.value: The Products screen.

data.name: T2.02.Name
data.value: Raw material

data.name: T2.02.Text
data.value: Material that goes into production. It usually comes from the supplier in sacks or boxes.

data.name: T2.02.InVyxum
data.value: The ingredient of each step in Formulation; its barcode is scanned.

data.name: T2.02.Example
data.value: Almonds, sugar, salt.

data.name: T2.03.Name
data.value: Finished product

data.name: T2.03.Text
data.value: The product that comes out of production, ready for sale.

data.name: T2.03.InVyxum
data.value: Waste calculation: how much finished product was packed from the raw material weighed.

data.name: T2.03.Example
data.value: A 250 g pack of mixed nuts.

data.name: T2.04.Name
data.value: Recipe (formula)

data.name: T2.04.Text
data.value: The list of which ingredients, and how much of each, go into a product. It is written for the standard batch size.

data.name: T2.04.InVyxum
data.value: The Recipes tab in Formulation.

data.name: T2.04.Example
data.value: In a 50 kg batch, 20 kg almonds, 15 kg hazelnuts…

data.name: T2.05.Name
data.value: Standard batch

data.name: T2.05.Text
data.value: The base quantity the recipe is written for. A larger or smaller batch is scaled from it.

data.name: T2.05.InVyxum
data.value: Ingredient target = standard quantity × (batch / standard batch).

data.name: T2.05.Example
data.value: Standard 50 kg, wanted 5 kg: every ingredient drops to a tenth.

data.name: T2.06.Name
data.value: Recipe version

data.name: T2.06.Text
data.value: Every change to a recipe makes a new version. States: draft, in approval, published (in use), old. A published version cannot be changed.

data.name: T2.06.InVyxum
data.value: The batch report shows which version was used.

data.name: T2.06.Example
data.value: R-014 version 4.

data.name: T2.07.Name
data.value: Formulation

data.name: T2.07.Text
data.value: Weighing ingredients one by one, in order, according to a recipe. The operator sees what to add and how much is left.

data.name: T2.07.InVyxum
data.value: The paid Formulation module.

data.name: T2.08.Name
data.value: Work order

data.name: T2.08.Text
data.value: The instruction "make this much of this product". Vyxum splits it into batches.

data.name: T2.08.InVyxum
data.value: In Formulation the operator picks it from "Today's jobs".

data.name: T2.08.Example
data.value: WO-0001: 250 pieces → 10 batches × 5 kg.

data.name: T2.09.Name
data.value: Batch (Formulation)

data.name: T2.09.Text
data.value: One complete weighing and mixing of a recipe. It is tracked by its number.

data.name: T2.09.InVyxum
data.value: The batch number has the form L-yyMMdd-sequence.

data.name: T2.09.Example
data.value: L-261121-05: the 5th batch of 21 November 2026.

data.name: T2.10.Name
data.value: Lot / raw material batch

data.name: T2.10.Text
data.value: The number of a group of goods made under the same conditions. For raw materials, it is the batch number on the supplier's sack.

data.name: T2.10.InVyxum
data.value: In Formulation it is read from the sack barcode and stored with the batch; tracing back uses it.

data.name: T2.10.Example
data.value: Almond sack lot 24-1187.

data.name: T2.11.Name
data.value: Container

data.name: T2.11.Text
data.value: The bucket or container the ingredients are weighed into.

data.name: T2.11.InVyxum
data.value: The "Take tare and start" step in Formulation.

data.name: T2.12.Name
data.value: Waste

data.name: T2.12.Text
data.value: The quantity lost in production: the difference between the raw material weighed and the finished product packed.

data.name: T2.12.InVyxum
data.value: The batch report.

data.name: T2.12.Example
data.value: 50 kg weighed, 49 kg packed: 2% waste.

data.name: T2.13.Name
data.value: Allergen

data.name: T2.13.Text
data.value: Substances that cause allergies in some people and must be highlighted on the label.

data.name: T2.13.InVyxum
data.value: A warning in the Formulation step; printed in bold on the label.

data.name: T2.13.Example
data.value: Hazelnuts, milk, gluten, sesame.

data.name: T2.14.Name
data.value: Cross-contamination

data.name: T2.14.Text
data.value: The chance that an allergen not in the product gets in, in small amounts, because the same machine or plant is used.

data.name: T2.14.InVyxum
data.value: The warning on the label; the cleaning confirmation in Formulation.

data.name: T2.14.Example
data.value: "May contain traces of peanuts."

data.name: T2.15.Name
data.value: Cleaning confirmation

data.name: T2.15.Text
data.value: If an allergen from the previous batch is not in the new recipe, the step where someone confirms the station was cleaned before starting.

data.name: T2.15.InVyxum
data.value: The ingredient weighing screen of Formulation.

data.name: T2.16.Name
data.value: Expiry date

data.name: T2.16.Text
data.value: The last day a raw material may be used.

data.name: T2.16.InVyxum
data.value: Formulation refuses an expired raw material.

data.name: T2.17.Name
data.value: Shelf life

data.name: T2.17.Text
data.value: How many days the product stays good after production. The date on the label is calculated from it.

data.name: T2.17.InVyxum
data.value: Date on the label = production date + shelf life.

data.name: T2.17.Example
data.value: Shelf life 180 days.

data.name: T2.18.Name
data.value: FEFO

data.name: T2.18.Text
data.value: First Expired, First Out: use the item with the nearest date first.

data.name: T2.19.Name
data.value: Traceability: tracing back and forward

data.name: T2.19.Text
data.value: Tracing back: which raw materials went into a batch? Tracing forward: which batches and labels did a raw material go into?

data.name: T2.19.InVyxum
data.value: Batches in Formulation, Printed in Labels.

data.name: T2.19.Example
data.value: Which 12 batches used the faulty almond lot?

data.name: T2.20.Name
data.value: Recall

data.name: T2.20.Text
data.value: Taking a faulty batch back from the market. You need to find quickly which cases and packages went where.

data.name: T2.20.InVyxum
data.value: In Labels, a recall list by batch number (cases, SSCCs, quantity).

data.name: T2.20.Example
data.value: Foreign matter in a batch: 48 cases are recalled.

data.name: T2.21.Name
data.value: Quarantine / on hold

data.name: T2.21.Text
data.value: Goods that must not be used or shipped until a decision is made.

data.name: T2.21.InVyxum
data.value: In Net weight control a failed batch is put on hold.

data.name: T2.22.Name
data.value: Consumption / stock deduction

data.name: T2.22.Text
data.value: Deducting the raw material used in production from stock.

data.name: T2.22.InVyxum
data.value: Can be sent to the ERP when a batch is finished.

data.name: S3.Title
data.value: Labels and barcodes

data.name: S3.Intro
data.value: Labels, GS1 barcodes, printers and food label rules.

data.name: T3.01.Name
data.value: GS1

data.name: T3.01.Text
data.value: The organisation that gives out barcode numbers worldwide and writes the barcode rules. All supermarket barcodes follow GS1 rules. Companies join their national GS1 office (GS1 Türkiye in Turkey).

data.name: T3.01.InVyxum
data.value: Once the GS1 company prefix is entered, GS1 barcodes and templates become available. Vyxum does not issue numbers; the company gets them from GS1.

data.name: T3.01.Example
data.value: A supermarket chain asks its supplier for GS1 case labels.

data.name: T3.02.Name
data.value: GS1 company prefix

data.name: T3.02.Text
data.value: The number prefix GS1 gives a company. All the company's barcode numbers start with it. 869 stands for Turkey.

data.name: T3.02.InVyxum
data.value: The company and GS1 details in the Labels module.

data.name: T3.02.Example
data.value: 8691234 (example).

data.name: T3.03.Name
data.value: GTIN

data.name: T3.03.Text
data.value: Global Trade Item Number: a product's unique number worldwide. The number in the 13-digit supermarket barcode is a GTIN-13; trade units such as cases use a 14-digit GTIN-14. The GTIN-14 of a variable weight product starts with 9.

data.name: T3.03.InVyxum
data.value: Product details in the Labels module.

data.name: T3.04.Name
data.value: EAN-13

data.name: T3.04.Text
data.value: The 13-digit barcode scanned at supermarket checkouts.

data.name: T3.04.InVyxum
data.value: The retail label: the GTIN for fixed weight products, with the weight embedded for weighed products.

data.name: T3.05.Name
data.value: Weight-embedded EAN-13

data.name: T3.05.Text
data.value: For weighed products the weight (or price) is put inside the barcode so the checkout knows it. Prefix 20 to 29 + PLU (5 digits) + weight in grams (5 digits) + check digit.

data.name: T3.05.InVyxum
data.value: The weighed retail template.

data.name: T3.06.Name
data.value: Check digit

data.name: T3.06.Text
data.value: The last digit of a barcode. It is calculated from the other digits and catches reading errors.

data.name: T3.06.InVyxum
data.value: Vyxum calculates it.

data.name: T3.07.Text
data.value: The long GS1 barcode used on case and logistics labels. It carries several pieces of data, separated by AIs.

data.name: T3.07.InVyxum
data.value: The GS1 case template; if it does not fit, Vyxum splits it into several barcodes.

data.name: T3.08.Name
data.value: AI (application identifier)

data.name: T3.08.Text
data.value: The code in brackets in front of each piece of data in a GS1 barcode; it says what the data after it is.

data.name: T3.08.InVyxum
data.value: Users do not type AIs; they tick the data to put in the barcode from a list.

data.name: T3.08.Example
data.value: (01) GTIN, (10) batch, (15) best before, (17) use by, (3103) net kg, (37) count, (00) SSCC.

data.name: T3.09.Name
data.value: FNC1

data.name: T3.09.Text
data.value: A special separator in GS1-128 that marks the end of a variable-length data field.

data.name: T3.09.InVyxum
data.value: Vyxum adds it.

data.name: T3.09.Example
data.value: It goes after the (10) batch number when another AI follows.

data.name: T3.10.Name
data.value: SSCC

data.name: T3.10.Text
data.value: Serial Shipping Container Code: the unique 18-digit serial number of each case or pallet. Extension digit + company prefix + serial number + check digit. A number is never used twice.

data.name: T3.10.InVyxum
data.value: The barcode at the bottom of the case label; the recall list.

data.name: T3.11.Name
data.value: DataMatrix

data.name: T3.11.Text
data.value: A small, square two-dimensional barcode. It holds a lot of data in little space. One written to GS1 rules is a GS1 DataMatrix.

data.name: T3.11.InVyxum
data.value: The batch label.

data.name: T3.12.Name
data.value: Code 128

data.name: T3.12.Text
data.value: A general-purpose barcode that can hold letters and digits. No GS1 membership is needed.

data.name: T3.12.InVyxum
data.value: On the container label when there is no GS1 prefix.

data.name: T3.13.Name
data.value: QR

data.name: T3.13.Text
data.value: A square barcode that phones can read.

data.name: T3.13.InVyxum
data.value: For free text or a link.

data.name: T3.14.Name
data.value: Quiet zone

data.name: T3.14.Text
data.value: The blank space that must be left on both sides of a barcode. The scanner uses it to find where the barcode starts.

data.name: T3.14.InVyxum
data.value: Taken into account when checking whether the barcode fits on the label.

data.name: T3.15.Name
data.value: X dimension (bar width)

data.name: T3.15.Text
data.value: The width of the narrowest bar in a barcode. A larger value makes the barcode longer but easier to read.

data.name: T3.15.InVyxum
data.value: Default 0.5 mm on the case label.

data.name: T3.16.Name
data.value: Scan test

data.name: T3.16.Text
data.value: Decoding the barcodes on the drawn label with scanning software and comparing them with the expected data.

data.name: T3.16.InVyxum
data.value: "4 / 4 barcodes read" in the template editor.

data.name: T3.17.Name
data.value: Label template

data.name: T3.17.Text
data.value: The layout of a label: size, what goes where, text size, barcode. The data comes from the product card. Its version goes up with every save.

data.name: T3.17.InVyxum
data.value: Templates and the template editor in the Labels module.

data.name: T3.17.Example
data.value: Weighed retail 100 × 60 mm.

data.name: T3.18.Name
data.value: Starter template

data.name: T3.18.Text
data.value: A ready draft with the required data that a new template starts from. You never start from a blank page.

data.name: T3.18.InVyxum
data.value: The "New template" screen.

data.name: T3.18.Example
data.value: GS1 case 100 × 150, Container label 58 × 40.

data.name: T3.19.Name
data.value: Retail label

data.name: T3.19.Text
data.value: The label on the pack the consumer buys: name, ingredients, net, price, date, barcode.

data.name: T3.19.InVyxum
data.value: "Save and print label" on the Weighing screen.

data.name: T3.20.Name
data.value: Case

data.name: T3.20.Text
data.value: The outer cardboard box that holds several packages. Goods go to shops and warehouses in cases. "Packs per case" is how many packages go in one case.

data.name: T3.20.InVyxum
data.value: Cases are counted automatically; when one is full its label is printed and a new case starts.

data.name: T3.20.Example
data.value: 12 packs per case; the case label prints after the 12th pack.

data.name: T3.21.Name
data.value: Case label

data.name: T3.21.Text
data.value: The logistics label on a case: the product inside, number of packs, total net, batch, date and SSCC, with GS1-128 barcodes.

data.name: T3.21.InVyxum
data.value: The GS1 case template.

data.name: T3.22.Name
data.value: Container label

data.name: T3.22.Text
data.value: The small label stuck on the container of a weighed ingredient: ingredient, raw material batch, net, step.

data.name: T3.22.InVyxum
data.value: Printed at every confirmation in Formulation when the option is on.

data.name: T3.23.Name
data.value: Batch label

data.name: T3.23.Text
data.value: The label printed when a Formulation batch is finished: product, recipe version, work order, net, allergens, raw material batches.

data.name: T3.23.InVyxum
data.value: Printed automatically when the batch is finished.

data.name: T3.24.Name
data.value: Pallet

data.name: T3.24.Text
data.value: The wooden base that cases are stacked on.

data.name: T3.25.Name
data.value: Reprint

data.name: T3.25.Text
data.value: Printing a creased or torn label again with the same number. The reason and the person are recorded.

data.name: T3.26.Name
data.value: ZPL / TSPL

data.name: T3.26.Text
data.value: Common command languages of label printers. No Windows driver is needed.

data.name: T3.26.InVyxum
data.value: Vyxum Agent talks to the printer in these languages.

data.name: T3.27.Name
data.value: dpi

data.name: T3.27.Text
data.value: The printer's dots per inch. 203 dpi is common; 300 dpi is sharper.

data.name: T3.27.InVyxum
data.value: The template resolution.

data.name: T3.28.Name
data.value: Thermal printer / ribbon

data.name: T3.28.Text
data.value: Label printers print with heat. Some use a ribbon; printing stops when the ribbon runs out.

data.name: T3.28.InVyxum
data.value: "Load paper" or a ribbon-out warning in the status area.

data.name: T3.29.Name
data.value: Virtual printer

data.name: T3.29.Text
data.value: Software that acts like a printer when there is no real one. It builds the commands but sends nothing, and keeps the output.

data.name: T3.29.InVyxum
data.value: The status area says "Sent" instead of "Printed". For training and trials.

data.name: T3.30.Name
data.value: Best before / use by date

data.name: T3.30.Text
data.value: Best before is a quality date; use by is a safety date for products that spoil quickly (see Most often confused). The full wording is printed on the label.

data.name: T3.30.InVyxum
data.value: Chosen per product; (15) and (17) in GS1.

data.name: T3.30.Example
data.value: Best before: 20.05.2027.

data.name: T3.31.Name
data.value: Nutrition declaration

data.name: T3.31.Text
data.value: The table of energy (kJ and kcal), fat, saturated fat, carbohydrate, sugars, protein and salt per 100 g.

data.name: T3.31.InVyxum
data.value: The nutrition table on the label.

data.name: T3.32.Name
data.value: Food business registration number

data.name: T3.32.Text
data.value: The number the Turkish Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry gives a food business. It must be on the label.

data.name: T3.32.InVyxum
data.value: The food label check looks for it.

data.name: T3.33.Name
data.value: Origin

data.name: T3.33.Text
data.value: The country or place the product or its main ingredient comes from.

data.name: T3.33.Example
data.value: Origin: Turkey.

data.name: T3.34.Name
data.value: Turkish Food Codex

data.name: T3.34.Text
data.value: The regulations that hold Turkey's food rules. The labelling regulation sets the required information and text sizes.

data.name: T3.34.InVyxum
data.value: The basis of the food label check.

data.name: T3.35.Name
data.value: x-height

data.name: T3.35.Text
data.value: The height of a lowercase "x". The regulation measures the smallest text on a label with it: at least 1.2 mm for required information, or 0.9 mm if the largest surface of the package is smaller than 80 cm². It is the package surface that counts, not the label size.

data.name: T3.35.InVyxum
data.value: The food label check measures text size by it.

data.name: T3.35.Example
data.value: 7 pt text ≈ 1.26 mm.

data.name: T3.36.Name
data.value: Food label check

data.name: T3.36.Text
data.value: Vyxum checks a template for required information, text size, barcode readability and fit. It only warns; the food engineer gives the final approval.

data.name: T3.36.InVyxum
data.value: The "2 warnings" line in the template editor.

data.name: S4.Title
data.value: Net weight control

data.name: S4.Intro
data.value: The language of the prepackage regulation: Qn, TNE, T1, T2.

data.name: T4.01.Name
data.value: Prepackage

data.name: T4.01.Text
data.value: A pack filled and closed without the customer present, whose contents cannot change without opening it.

data.name: T4.01.InVyxum
data.value: What Net weight control checks.

data.name: T4.01.Example
data.value: A 250 g pack of nuts.

data.name: T4.02.Name
data.value: Fixed quantity / variable weight

data.name: T4.02.Text
data.value: With fixed quantity every pack says the same amount (250 g). With variable weight each pack is weighed and priced (1.248 kg).

data.name: T4.02.InVyxum
data.value: Net weight control works only with fixed quantity products.

data.name: T4.03.Name
data.value: Prepackage regulation (76/211/EEC)

data.name: T4.03.Text
data.value: The Turkish regulation on determining the net quantity of prepackages. It matches the European directive 76/211/EEC.

data.name: T4.03.InVyxum
data.value: The rules of Net weight control are based on it.

data.name: T4.04.Name
data.value: Qn (nominal quantity)

data.name: T4.04.Text
data.value: The quantity printed on the label.

data.name: T4.04.InVyxum
data.value: A separate field from the fill target on the plan screen.

data.name: T4.05.Name
data.value: Fill target

data.name: T4.05.Text
data.value: The quantity the filling machine aims for; usually a little more than Qn.

data.name: T4.05.InVyxum
data.value: Vyxum suggests a fill target but does not set the machine.

data.name: T4.06.Name
data.value: Overfill

data.name: T4.06.Text
data.value: Product put into packs beyond Qn. It is not a legal problem, but it costs money.

data.name: T4.06.InVyxum
data.value: The cost of overfill in the batch details.

data.name: T4.06.Example
data.value: +3 g per pack × 1,000 packs = 3 kg of free product.

data.name: T4.07.Name
data.value: TNE

data.name: T4.07.Text
data.value: Tolerable negative error: how much less than Qn a pack may contain. It is calculated from Qn using the table in the regulation, not typed in.

data.name: T4.07.InVyxum
data.value: Calculated on the plan screen.

data.name: T4.07.Example
data.value: Qn 250 g → TNE 9 g.

data.name: T4.08.Name
data.value: T1

data.name: T4.08.Text
data.value: T1 = Qn − TNE. A pack below this limit is "short". The number of short packs in a batch is limited.

data.name: T4.08.InVyxum
data.value: "Short, below T1" in the status area.

data.name: T4.09.Name
data.value: T2

data.name: T4.09.Text
data.value: T2 = Qn − 2 × TNE. A pack below this limit is "far too short" and must not reach the market. Even one is a reason to stop the line.

data.name: T4.09.InVyxum
data.value: "Stop" in the status area; the batch is put on hold and needs a supervisor's approval.

data.name: T4.10.Name
data.value: ℮ mark

data.name: T4.10.Text
data.value: The small "e" on the label: it declares that the pack was filled by the regulation's procedure. It is optional, but packs that carry it must follow the rules.

data.name: T4.10.InVyxum
data.value: No ℮-marked label is printed for a pack below T2.

data.name: T4.11.Name
data.value: Three conditions

data.name: T4.11.Text
data.value: For a batch to pass: (1) the mean is high enough, (2) the number of packs below T1 is within the limit, (3) no pack is below T2.

data.name: T4.11.InVyxum
data.value: Three lines on the quality screen, each "met" or "not met".

data.name: T4.12.Name
data.value: Batch (Net weight)

data.name: T4.12.Text
data.value: The group of packs judged together under the regulation: same product, line and place. At the end of a line, at most one hour of production; otherwise at most 10,000 packs.

data.name: T4.12.InVyxum
data.value: Batch type on the plan screen: hourly or production lot.

data.name: T4.12.Example
data.value: A line making 360 packs an hour: one batch every hour.

data.name: T4.13.Name
data.value: Sampling / sampling plan

data.name: T4.13.Text
data.value: Deciding by weighing a set number of packs instead of the whole batch. The batch size decides how many.

data.name: T4.13.InVyxum
data.value: Vyxum spreads the sample over the hour: 30 packs → 10 packs every 20 minutes.

data.name: T4.13.Example
data.value: Batch of 100–500 packs: 30 packs.

data.name: T4.14.Name
data.value: Acceptance and rejection number / second sample

data.name: T4.14.Text
data.value: The number of packs below T1 allowed in a sample. Up to the acceptance number it passes; from the rejection number it fails; in between a second sample is taken.

data.name: T4.14.InVyxum
data.value: "Start second sample" at the station.

data.name: T4.14.Example
data.value: Sample of 30 with 1 short: passes; 2 short: second sample; 3 short: fails.

data.name: T4.15.Name
data.value: Non-destructive / destructive testing

data.name: T4.15.Text
data.value: In non-destructive testing the pack is weighed unopened and the average packaging weight is subtracted as tare. In destructive testing the pack is opened.

data.name: T4.15.InVyxum
data.value: Vyxum uses the non-destructive method.

data.name: T4.16.Name
data.value: Tare sample

data.name: T4.16.Text
data.value: Weighing a few empty packs at the start of a shift and using their average as the tare for that shift.

data.name: T4.16.InVyxum
data.value: The tare step at the station: 6 / 10.

data.name: T4.16.Example
data.value: 10 empty bags, average 12 g.

data.name: T4.17.Name
data.value: Mean criterion (k factor)

data.name: T4.17.Text
data.value: The statistical formula for the sample mean to be enough: x̄ ≥ Qn − k · s. k is a fixed number that depends on the sample size.

data.name: T4.17.InVyxum
data.value: Only on the quality screen; the operator does no calculation.

data.name: T4.18.Name
data.value: Pass / pass with warning / fail

data.name: T4.18.Text
data.value: The batch result. With warning: the conditions are met but the mean is below Qn; the next check is brought forward.

data.name: T4.18.InVyxum
data.value: The batch list and the compliance report.

data.name: T4.19.Name
data.value: Sort / refill / destroy

data.name: T4.19.Text
data.value: The decision options for a failed batch. Sorting means weighing every pack and taking out the short ones.

data.name: T4.19.InVyxum
data.value: The decision form, with an electronic signature.

data.name: T4.20.Name
data.value: Trend warning

data.name: T4.20.Text
data.value: A rule that gives early warning that the filling machine is drifting when short packs become more frequent.

data.name: T4.20.InVyxum
data.value: "3 short in the last 10 packs. Check the filling machine."

data.name: T4.21.Name
data.value: Compliance report

data.name: T4.21.Text
data.value: The report for the inspector, showing the batch results, the method and the signatures.

data.name: T4.21.InVyxum
data.value: Available as PDF and Excel.

data.name: T4.22.Name
data.value: Metrology / legal metrology

data.name: T4.22.Text
data.value: Metrology is the science of measurement. Legal metrology is the state's rules for measurements used in trade. In Turkey, quantity inspection belongs to the Ministry of Industry and Technology.

data.name: T4.23.Name
data.value: WELMEC / OIML

data.name: T4.23.Text
data.value: The European (WELMEC) and international (OIML) legal metrology organisations. They publish guidance documents.

data.name: T4.24.Name
data.value: Checkweigher

data.name: T4.24.Text
data.value: An automatic checking scale on the line that weighs every pack and rejects the short ones.

data.name: S5.Title
data.value: Quality, records and reports

data.name: S5.Intro
data.value: Record and approval terms that auditors ask about.

data.name: T5.01.Name
data.value: Four-eyes principle

data.name: T5.01.Text
data.value: The person who did a task cannot approve it; a second person checks.

data.name: T5.01.InVyxum
data.value: Whoever wrote a recipe cannot approve it. It can be turned off in the settings; on by default.

data.name: T5.02.Name
data.value: Electronic signature

data.name: T5.02.Text
data.value: An approval recorded with name, time and meaning after the person enters their password again. The electronic version of a handwritten signature.

data.name: T5.02.InVyxum
data.value: Recipe approval, net weight batch approval and decision.

data.name: T5.02.Example
data.value: "Recipe approval, R-014 version 4".

data.name: T5.03.Name
data.value: Supervisor approval / PIN

data.name: T5.03.Text
data.value: When a rule has to be broken (outside tolerance, below T2), the shift supervisor allows it with a short code and a reason.

data.name: T5.03.InVyxum
data.value: The small, locked "Supervisor approval" button under the main button.

data.name: T5.04.Name
data.value: Audit trail

data.name: T5.04.Text
data.value: A list that cannot be deleted of who changed what, and when.

data.name: T5.04.InVyxum
data.value: Records are only ever added; even a cancellation is a mark, not a deletion.

data.name: T5.05.Name
data.value: Hash chain / record integrity

data.name: T5.05.Text
data.value: Each record carries a fingerprint of the one before it. If someone changes an old record, the chain breaks and it is noticed.

data.name: T5.05.InVyxum
data.value: The "Record integrity broken" warning.

data.name: T5.06.Name
data.value: GMP

data.name: T5.06.Text
data.value: Good Manufacturing Practice: quality rules that are mandatory especially in pharmaceuticals.

data.name: T5.07.Name
data.value: 21 CFR Part 11 / EU GMP Annex 11

data.name: T5.07.Text
data.value: The US (FDA) and EU rules for electronic records and electronic signatures. Pharmaceutical companies expect software to follow them.

data.name: T5.08.Name
data.value: Validation

data.name: T5.08.Text
data.value: Proving with documents that the software works as intended. Pharmaceutical companies require it.

data.name: T5.09.Name
data.value: End of day

data.name: T5.09.Text
data.value: A summary of the day's weighings: number of records, total net, total amount, cancellations.

data.name: T5.09.InVyxum
data.value: The paid Reporting module.

data.name: T5.10.Name
data.value: Z report

data.name: T5.10.Text
data.value: A term from cash registers: the closing report that gives the day's totals and resets the counters. An interim report without reset is an X report.

data.name: T5.10.InVyxum
data.value: The paid Reporting module.

data.name: T5.10.Example
data.value: The Z report is taken at 18:00; the next day the counters start from zero.

data.name: T5.11.Name
data.value: Period closing

data.name: T5.11.Text
data.value: Finalising and reporting the records of a period (day, week, month).

data.name: T5.11.InVyxum
data.value: The paid Reporting module.

data.name: T5.12.Name
data.value: Shift

data.name: T5.12.Text
data.value: A working period (for example 08:00–16:00). The tare sample and some batches start and end with the shift.

data.name: S6.Title
data.value: Screens and use

data.name: S6.Intro
data.value: Ideas that come up often on the screens.

data.name: T6.01.Name
data.value: Operator

data.name: T6.01.Text
data.value: The person weighing at a station. Often gloved, standing and in a hurry; the screens are kept simple for them.

data.name: T6.01.InVyxum
data.value: The Operator column on the Records screen.

data.name: T6.02.Name
data.value: Shift supervisor / quality manager

data.name: T6.02.Text
data.value: The shift supervisor runs the line and gives supervisor approvals. The quality manager writes the plans and approves batches.

data.name: T6.02.InVyxum
data.value: Permissions in the Users and roles module.

data.name: T6.03.Name
data.value: Status area

data.name: T6.03.Text
data.value: The largest coloured area on an operator screen: colour, icon and one word. It tells what is happening in three seconds.

data.name: T6.03.InVyxum
data.value: "Printed", "Short", "Stop", "OK".

data.name: T6.04.Name
data.value: Go / OK / stop colours

data.name: T6.04.Text
data.value: The three colours of the status area: go (there is work to do), OK (good), stop (there is a problem). Colour never carries the meaning alone; there is always an icon and a word.

data.name: T6.05.Name
data.value: Main button

data.name: T6.05.Text
data.value: The single large button on every operator screen. It is always in the same place; when it is closed it says what is missing.

data.name: T6.05.InVyxum
data.value: "Save and print label", "Add 258 g more".

data.name: T6.06.Name
data.value: Focus mode

data.name: T6.06.Text
data.value: A screen where the left menu is hidden and only the current job shows. You leave it with "Pause".

data.name: T6.06.InVyxum
data.value: Formulation ingredient weighing and the net weight station.

data.name: T6.07.Name
data.value: Appearance: light, dark, large touch

data.name: T6.07.Text
data.value: The three appearances of the screen. In large touch, buttons and rows grow big enough to press with gloves.

data.name: T6.08.Name
data.value: Automatic printing / automatic saving

data.name: T6.08.Text
data.value: Saving and printing the label as soon as the weight is stable, without pressing a button.

data.name: T6.08.InVyxum
data.value: The Labels and Net weight stations.

data.name: T6.09.Name
data.value: Poka-yoke

data.name: T6.09.Text
data.value: Japanese for "mistake-proofing": design that makes the wrong action impossible.

data.name: T6.09.InVyxum
data.value: "Confirm" stays closed for the wrong raw material or outside the band.

data.name: T6.10.Name
data.value: Locked preview

data.name: T6.10.Text
data.value: A paid module without a license shows as locked in the menu; clicking it shows a blurred sample image and a "Request a trial license" button.

data.name: T6.10.InVyxum
data.value: Under "Vyxum Pro" in the menu.

data.name: S7.Title
data.value: ERP and license

data.name: S7.Intro
data.value: Connecting to the accounting system, and the Vyxum license.

data.name: T7.01.Name
data.value: ERP

data.name: T7.01.Text
data.value: The main system that runs a company's stock, production, sales and accounting.

data.name: T7.01.InVyxum
data.value: The integration module sends weighing results to the ERP.

data.name: T7.02.Name
data.value: Integration / connector

data.name: T7.02.Text
data.value: The module that carries data between Vyxum and the ERP. A connector is the part made for one specific ERP.

data.name: T7.02.InVyxum
data.value: A paid module.

data.name: T7.03.Name
data.value: Field mapping

data.name: T7.03.Text
data.value: Linking a field in Vyxum to the matching field in the ERP. It is done on a screen, without writing code.

data.name: T7.03.InVyxum
data.value: A screen of the integration module.

data.name: T7.03.Example
data.value: Vyxum "batch" → ERP "serial/lot no".

data.name: T7.04.Name
data.value: Item card

data.name: T7.04.Text
data.value: The product or raw material record in the ERP. The counterpart of the product card in Vyxum.

data.name: T7.04.InVyxum
data.value: Can be imported from the ERP into Vyxum.

data.name: T7.05.Name
data.value: Production order

data.name: T7.05.Text
data.value: The "make this" document opened in the ERP. The counterpart of the work order in Vyxum.

data.name: T7.06.Name
data.value: Slips: production receipt, consumption, waste, reversal

data.name: T7.06.Text
data.value: Documents that record stock movements in the ERP. A production receipt adds finished goods to stock, consumption deducts raw material, waste records losses, a reversal cancels.

data.name: T7.06.InVyxum
data.value: Sent from Vyxum to the ERP; by default all at once when a batch closes.

data.name: T7.07.Name
data.value: License file (.vxlic)

data.name: T7.07.Text
data.value: A signed file that says which modules the company may use, on how many stations and until when. It is verified without the internet.

data.name: T7.07.InVyxum
data.value: Settings > Modules and license; it unlocks paid modules without reinstalling.

data.name: T7.08.Name
data.value: Per-station license

data.name: T7.08.Text
data.value: Price and limits are based on the number of workplaces with a scale.

data.name: T7.08.InVyxum
data.value: Paid modules are licensed by the number of stations.

data.name: T7.09.Name
data.value: Trial license / grace period

data.name: T7.09.Text
data.value: A trial license unlocks paid modules for a limited time. The grace period is the time given after a license ends before the module becomes read-only. No data is deleted.

data.name: T7.09.InVyxum
data.value: "Request a trial license" in the locked preview; a warning strip at the top of the screen during the grace period.

data.name: T7.10.Name
data.value: Open core / Vyxum Pro

data.name: T7.10.Text
data.value: The free, open-source core (weighing, records, products) and the paid modules unlocked with a license on top of it (Labels, Formulation, Net weight…).

data.name: T7.10.InVyxum
data.value: Paid modules are under "Vyxum Pro" in the menu.

data.name: S8.Title
data.value: Connecting scales and printers

data.name: S8.Intro
data.value: Hardware words from the setup wizard and the Devices screen.

data.name: T8.01.Name
data.value: Serial port / COM / RS232

data.name: T8.01.Text
data.value: An old but common cable connection between scale and computer. In Windows it shows up with names like COM1 or COM3.

data.name: T8.01.InVyxum
data.value: A device setting; the operator screen does not show the port name.

data.name: T8.01.Example
data.value: Scale → COM3.

data.name: T8.02.Name
data.value: Baud, parity, stop bits (8N1)

data.name: T8.02.Text
data.value: The speed and format settings of a serial connection. If the two ends do not use the same settings, the data comes out as nonsense. 9600 8N1 is a common setting.

data.name: T8.02.InVyxum
data.value: The setup wizard and the Devices screen; common settings are tried while searching for the scale.

data.name: T8.03.Name
data.value: TCP/IP, port 9100

data.name: T8.03.Text
data.value: A network connection. Label printers on a network usually take commands on port 9100.

data.name: T8.03.InVyxum
data.value: Printers and scales can also connect over the network.

data.name: T8.04.Name
data.value: Vyxum Agent

data.name: T8.04.Text
data.value: A small program on the computer the scale and printer are connected to. It carries weights to the server and labels from the server to the printer.

data.name: T8.04.InVyxum
data.value: Runs as a Windows service.

data.name: T8.05.Name
data.value: Protocol

data.name: T8.05.Text
data.value: The format in which the scale sends the weight. Some scales answer when asked; others send the weight continuously.

data.name: T8.05.InVyxum
data.value: Choose the protocol that fits your scale in the device settings.

data.name: T8.06.Name
data.value: Simulator

data.name: T8.06.Text
data.value: A pretend scale that produces weights when there is no real one. For trials, training and demos.

data.name: T8.06.InVyxum
data.value: Connection type "Simulator" in the device settings.
